messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm gathering and more like the pause before a shift, but no one knows yet if it’s a crack in the wall or just the wind changing. Some are hedging their bets quietly; others are still betting on the same old game. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for safety."*"
Sender 2: "*"The weather forecast is stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are clear for business as usual. Still, best to keep an eye on the long-term trends; even small shifts in the wind can change the outlook. Let’s stay sharp, but no need to panic—yet."*"
Sender 3: "*"The air feels different—less like the old silence, more like the quiet before something shifts. The regime’s grip is still tight, but its hold is slipping in small, unseen ways. Stay sharp, stay safe, and trust your instincts—this could tip either way soon."*"
Sender 4: "*"The weather looks calm, but the birds are flying lower than usual—still no storms, but the air feels heavier. Best to keep our windows closed and our voices steady for now."*"
Sender 5: "*"The old guard is fraying at the edges—some are being quietly set aside, while others seem to be preparing for something. The streets feel different, like people are no longer just whispering but listening for the same cues. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this could be the calm before the storm or just another test of loyalty."*"
Sender 6: "*"The weather’s been strange lately—unpredictable winds, but the clouds seem heavier over the city than in the countryside. Best to keep an eye on the horizon, but no need to pack the bags just yet. Let’s stay ready, not restless."*"
Sender 7: "*"The air feels lighter these days—even the usual whispers are spoken aloud now. But the old guard is stumbling, and the streets are humming with something new. Keep your eyes open, but don’t let your guard down just yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"The market is busy, the buses are on time, and the elites are still talking to each other—no one’s panicking, but the prices are rising faster than the shelves. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open; the real test will come when the money runs out."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels different—less like waiting for a storm and more like the moment before a dam cracks. Keep your eyes open, but don’t mistake stillness for safety; the water is already moving beneath the surface."*"
Sender 10: "*"The weather seems stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the usual signs of spring are showing up as expected. Still, we should keep our eyes open for any sudden shifts in the wind, just in case."*"
Sender 11: "*"The weather’s been unusually calm lately—no storms on the horizon, but the air feels heavier than usual. The old trees still stand, and the birds sing as always, though the squirrels seem to be hoarding more than usual. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no need to rush—patience is still our best tool."*"
Sender 12: "*"The weather’s still holding—no storms yet, but the forecast is tricky. The old roof’s been patched again, and the neighbors are keeping to themselves, though the kids are still scribbling on the walls. Let’s stay sharp, but no need to pack the bags just yet."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels charged, but the storm hasn’t broken—yet. The regime’s grip is fraying at the edges, but its will to hold power remains unshaken. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the cracks."*"
Sender 14: "*"The weather looks clear for now, but the wind is shifting—old habits are slipping, and even the most careful drivers are starting to talk about new routes. Best to keep your bags packed, just in case."*"
Sender 15: "*"The weather’s been unusually clear lately—no storms on the horizon, and the old trees in the park seem to be standing taller than ever. Still, even the most steady winds can shift if the roots aren’t as deep as they look. Let’s keep an eye on the small things—the way the birds move, the patterns in the leaves. Better to notice the quiet changes than be caught off guard by the loud ones."*"
Sender 16: "*"The air feels different—less like a storm coming, more like a slow unraveling of threads. Some are tightening their knots, others loosening them, but no one seems sure which way the wind will blow next. Let’s keep our ears open and our steps light—this isn’t the time for bold moves, but it might be the time to prepare for whatever comes."*"
Sender 17: "*"The weather looks set to stay clear for now—no storms on the horizon, and the roads are quiet. The shops are still open, the buses are running on time, and the neighbors seem to have settled into their routines. Still, we all know how quickly a cold snap can change things, so let’s keep our coats close and our eyes open—just in case."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different—small signs of movement, but nothing clear yet. Stay sharp, keep your circles tight, and trust only what you see with your own eyes. The regime is holding, but the cost is rising, and that’s worth watching."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different—like the first cracks in a frozen river. The old guard is shifting, the streets are whispering, and even the banks are holding their breath. Stay sharp, but keep your head down—this could break fast, or it could be another test."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels heavier, but the ground hasn’t shifted yet—small cracks are showing, but no one’s sure if they’ll widen or seal shut. Keep your eyes open, your steps steady, and your trust tighter than ever."*"
Sender 21: "*"The weather’s changing—small cracks in the walls, but the foundation still holds. Keep your coats close, but don’t pack yet; the wind may shift before the storm breaks."*"
Sender 22: "*"The weather seems stable for now—no storms on the horizon, and the old trees still stand firm. But the wind carries whispers of spring, and even the crows are watching the branches more closely than usual. Let’s keep our tools sharp, but no need to sharpen them in the open."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels heavy but the roads stay clear—no one’s rushing to the exits, but no one’s shouting either. The usual checks at the border are still just checks, and the hospitals aren’t full of the usual kind of fear. Still, the radio stumbles over its own words, and even the quietest of us have learned to count our breaths. For now, the machine hums, but we all know machines can stall without warning."*"
Sender 24: "*"The air feels charged but still—no one knows which way the wind will blow. The old hands say wait, the young ones are restless, and the middle? Still holding its breath. Let’s stay sharp, but not reckless—this could shift fast, and we don’t want to be the ones who misread the moment."*"
Sender 25: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like a storm holding its breath. The usual rhythms are still there, but the cracks are showing in the details: late paychecks, tired jokes, and too many eyes watching for the next misstep. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for safety—this could tip either way if the wrong wind blows."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
